{{short description|Belgian mathematician (born 1976)}}
{{BLP primary sources|date=September 2025}}
'''Stefaan Vaes''' (born February 29, 1976, in [[Herentals]], [[Belgium]]) is a Belgian mathematician.
[[File: Vaes stefaan.jpg|thumb|Stefaan Vaes, [[Oberwolfach Research Institute for Mathematics|Oberwolfach]], 2015]]
Vaes studied mathematics at [[Katholieke Universiteit Leuven|KU Leuven]] with a diploma in 1998 and a PhD in 2001 with thesis advisor Alfons Van Daele and thesis Locally Compact Quantum Groups.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=117021}}</ref> As a postdoc, he worked from 1998 to 2002 at KU Leuven and from 1998 to 2002 in Paris, where he did research for [[CNRS]]. In 2002, he began part-time teaching at KU Leuven, where he became an associate professor in 2006 and a full professor in 2009.<ref name=CV>{{cite web|title=Homepage Stefaan Vaes, C.V.|url=https://sites.google.com/view/stefaan-vaes/cv}}</ref>

He was a visiting professor in 2009 at [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] (Paris VI) and in 2011 at [[Paris Diderot University]] (Paris VII) (where he habilitated in 2004). In 2005, he held the ''Peccot Chair'' at the [[Collège de France]].<ref name=CV/>

His research deals with [[Von Neumann algebra]]s and [[quantum group]]s.

In 2010, Vaes was an invited speaker with a talk on ''Rigidity for von Neumann algebras and their invariants'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Hyderabad]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Vaes, Stefaan|chapter=Rigidity for von Neumann algebras and their invariants|title=''In:'' Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians 2010 (ICM 2010) (In 4 Volumes) Vol. I: Plenary Lectures and Ceremonies Vols. II–IV: Invited Lectures|volume=III|pages=1624–1650|year=2010|doi=10.1142/9789814324359_0113|arxiv=1008.3610 |isbn=978-981-4324-30-4|s2cid=119610699 }} [https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.3610 arXiv preprint]</ref> In 2012, he was elected a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]. In 2015, he received the [[Francqui Prize]].

His doctoral students include {{ill|Cyril Houdayer|de}}.
